question.leadin: This ruler bore Caesarion while serving as Julius Caesar's mistress.
question.text: Who is this female Egyptian pharaoh from the Ptolemy dynasty who notably killed herself with a snakebite?
question.clue: Drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar apocryphally won a bet for this ruler, whose short-lived successor was Caesarion.

swap.leadin: This son of Akhenaten ruled with the assistance of the vizier Ay ("eye"), who eventually succeeded him after his death.
swap.text: Name this "Boy Pharaoh" of Egypt, whose tomb was famously discovered nearly intact by Howard Carter.
swap.clue: This pharaoh moved Egypt's capital back to Thebes from Amarna and reinstated the worship of traditional Egyptian gods.

question.leadin: This ruler's capital at Amarna was discovered by Flinders Petrie, and his wife was Nefertiti.
question.text: Name this 18th dynasty pharaoh who attempted to establish monotheistic sun worship.
question.clue: Like his father, who married a non-royal woman named Tiy, he married a woman who was not of royal blood, the daughter of a vizier named Ay.

swap.text: King Tut's tomb was discovered by this man who lost many comrades, including expedition leader Lord Carnarvon, after an alleged "mummy's curse".
swap.clue: Starting at age 17, this person worked for Gaston Maspero, who provided a recommendation for a later employer.

question.leadin: Antipater of Sidon listed one of this site's structures as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: Name this site of the Great Pyramids, located just outside Cairo.
question.clue: The greatest wonders you beheld were the three pyramids of this city, the largest of which was built by the great pharaoh Khufu.

swap.text: Two answers required. These two portions of Ancient Egypt were united in the First Dynasty. They are represented by a red crown and a white crown.

question.leadin: During the Byzantine period, this city was known primarily for its production of silk.
question.text: Name this Greek city in Boeotia. Its central fortress was known as the Cadmea after its mythical founder, and its army was notably led by Epaminondas.
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.leadin: In ancient Egypt, the vizier was the head official and top advisor in the pharaoh's court.
swap.text: Perhaps the most significant early vizier was this man, who served under Djoser. Best known for his architectural work during his life, he was later deified as the god of medicine.
swap.clue: The great Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara is attributed to this minister and polymath, later deified as a god of medicine, who also completed projects abandoned by Sekhemkhet.

question.leadin: Under this ruler, Egypt switched from using sun-dried bricks in large constructions to more durable limestone.
question.text: Name this ruler of the 3rd Dynasty who ordered the construction of Egypt's first pyramid, the Step Pyramid.
question.clue: An official of this pharaoh communes with the god Khnum to stop a seven-year flood, as recorded on the Famine Stela.

swap.text: This pharaoh of the fourth dynasty went pyramid-crazy, constructing the Medium, Red and Bent Pyramids.
swap.clue: This ruler was married to Hetepheres I, and he likely built the Praise of the Two Lands ship.

question.leadin: The word aamu may refer to these people during their early contacts.
question.text: Name these people who invaded Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period. These people, who introduced the chariot to Egypt, constituted Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty.
question.clue: In a satirical story, a ruler of these people complains that he can't sleep because of noisy hippos in a letter addressed to Seqenenre ("sek-en-EN-ray") Tao.

swap.leadin: CAN BE READ TO ANY TEAM This culture was conquered by the Hyksos ("HICK-sohs") from Western Asia, who set up a capital at Avaris.
swap.text: Name this culture that built pyramids along the Nile River.
swap.clue: This civilization was ruled from Amarna by the husband of Nefertiti.

question.leadin: Emperor Claudius wrote a letter to the inhabitants of a city in this province about Jewish freedom of worship.
question.text: Name this region that became a Roman province a decade after its Queen Arsinoe was executed in Rome.
question.clue: By the 1st century C.E. this province produced the largest share of the cura annonae.

swap.text: The existence of this pharaoh is attested to by a namesake palette that depicts him with two crowns. This pharaoh was the unifier of Upper and Lower Egypt.
swap.clue: This pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.

question.text: The so-called "0 Dynasty" ends and the First Dynasty begins with Narmer unifying these two regions. The Narmer Palette found at Hierakonpolis shows him wearing the red and white crowns of these two regions.
question.answerHtml: Upper Egypt and Lower Egypt [accept Upper and Lower Egypt; accept the Sedge and the Bee]
question.clue: One of them had a name meaning "Land of the Reeds," the other was called the "Land of the North," and the two were collectively called Tawy("tah-wee").

swap.leadin: Researchers determined that a "screaming mummy" discovered next to the body of a pharaoh of this name was his son Pentawere, who had been forced to hang himself over his role in an assassination plot.
swap.text: Give this name of the pharaoh targeted by Pentawere's mother, Tiye, in the "harem conspiracy." An earlier pharaoh with this name commissioned the temples at Abu Simbel ("AH-boo SEEM-bel") and won the Battle of Kadesh ("kah-DESH").
swap.answerHtml: Ramesses [ accept Ramesses the Great or Ramesses II; accept Ramesses III; accept Ramses in place of “Ramesses”; prompt on Ozymandias]
swap.clue: An earlier ruler with this name fought a battle on the Orontes River against the forces of Muwatalli II, which is depicted in sculptures at the Abu Simbel complex.

question.text: The pyramid at el-Lahun, or Kahun, was designed for the second pharaoh of this name, who also built a great dike there. Except for its last female ruler Sobekneferu, the entire Twelfth Dynasty consisted only of pharaohs with this name or Amenemhat.
question.clue: This name of three Twelfth Dynasty pharaohs. Herodotus gave this name's Greek equivalent to a pharaoh who supposedly erected genitalia-topped columns to mock the cities he conquered in Asia Minor and Thrace.

swap.leadin: The Tomb of the Warriors in this man's mortuary temple is believed to contain the remains of warriors who died heroically as this king fought to reunify Egypt.
swap.text: Name this member of the 11th Dynasty and first pharaoh of the Middle Kingdom. This man's mortuary temple at Deir-el-Bahari, which contained a small pyramid at its top, inspired the neighboring one dedicated to Hatshepsut.

question.text: Though most Egyptologists agree that ancient Egyptians were not black, they are certain that pharaohs from this dynasty were black. This last dynasty in the Third Intermediate Period lasted from 760 BC to 656 BC, and its fall marked the beginning of the Late Period.

swap.leadin: Name these men involved in the power struggle after the death of Alexander the Great, FTPE.
swap.text: He finally put down the ambitious campaigns of Perdiccas and seized the body of Alexander to stake his claim to the empire, though he eventually encouraged the dissolution of the empire and settled for just being King of Egypt.
swap.clue: He acquired his first wife Artacama during the mass wedding at Susa, cemented a later alliance by marrying Antipater's daughter Eurydice, and finally chose another wife, Berenice, to elevate to the title of queen.
